summary: Lumenary Diagnostics: concurrent session-resume jitter and KV-prefix divergence causing incoherent resumed responses
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10T01:12Z Lumenary reported users observing incoherent resumptions during multi-turn streaming sessions. When a mobile client reconnected (normal network flaps), resumed completions merged with new token streams producing garbled text and occasional hallucinated metadata. Impact: customer-facing clinical triage assistant returned malformed results affecting ~7% of sessions during the morning peak window (01:00-03:00 UTC). Environment: production, us-east, enterprise account with reserved dedicated pool and session-affinity configured. This ticket tracks the Major Incident, escalations with the customer, the immediate mitigations, and post-incident follow-up items.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running chat (context > 1024 tokens) against redwood-v2-13b via streaming API with session-affinity enabled.
2) Induce a network interruption from a client (simulate cellular handoff) and reconnect within 3-8 seconds.
3) Observe resumed stream: tokens from prior prefix are replayed and interleaved with newly generated tokens leading to partial sentence fragments and mismatched entity references.
4) Check serving logs for overlapping KV write timestamps and socket reconnect events correlated to the same session_id.

timeline: 2026-03-10 01:12 UTC - Lumenary support engineer escalates via support@redwood. High volume of malformed resumptions observed.
2026-03-10 01:20 UTC - Triage: Support assigns to SRE on-call (Jonas Klein). Initial hypothesis: session-affinity race during socket reconnect.
2026-03-10 01:45 UTC - Metric spike: apparent KV write rate for session-affinity namespace increased 4x; tail-latency 95p rose from 80ms to 420ms.
2026-03-10 02:10 UTC - Engineering patch: disabled optimistic KV write parallelism for session restore on the dedicated pool; enabled conservative session lock for in-flight resumption.
2026-03-10 02:25 UTC - Mitigation validated with Lumenary on test traffic; malformed resumes dropped from ~7% to <0.1%.
2026-03-10 03:00 UTC - Issue declared resolved for production traffic; follow-up items created for root cause analysis and longer-term fix.
comments: Support (Amira): Customer reported incoherent merged tokens across resumed sessions. They provided sample session IDs and example transcripts. Customer is highly sensitive — clinical assistant. Escalated to P0.

SRE (Jonas): Observed overlapping KV writes and reconnects for same session_id. Reproducer created in staging. Temporary mitigation: disable optimistic write-ahead for session restore and apply short session lock. Rolling to dedicated pool now.
Customer (Lumenary): Thank you for rapid response. Can you confirm there will be no data loss? Our compliance team is on standby.

Eng (Maya Chen): Patch PR opened to ensure single-writer guarantees on session restore path and to add sequence-number checks for KV-store merges. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2411
SRE (Jonas): Hotfix rolled at 02:10 UTC. Observability dashboards show normalized resume success rate. Scheduling RCA and postmortem owners.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Socket-level reconnects were being handled by different serving nodes before KV prefix write was durable, leading to inconsistent prefix state on resume.

Hypothesis 2: Under bursty reconnect patterns the KV-store write-ahead buffer allowed two writers to commit overlapping prefix ranges; merge logic assumed idempotency which is false for partial token boundaries.

Findings: Trace correlation of socket reconnect and KV write events shows <200ms window where two processes accepted writes for the same session_id with adjacent sequence offsets. The merge routine did not enforce sequence continuity checks, producing token interleaving.

Observed contributing factor: recent kernel selection tweak (auto-batch aggressiveness) increased parallelism for prefix writes on quantized models leading to slightly higher concurrency on the critical path.

Telemetry: Affected sessions concentrated on customers using mobile clients behind NAT with frequent ephemeral IP changes; the dedicated pool routing and session-affinity TTL allowed reconnects to land on different workers.
resolution: Hotfix deployed: disabled optimistic KV parallel writes for session restore, enabled conservative session-level locks for resumptions, and added sequence continuity validation in merge logic. Post-deploy monitoring confirmed reduction of malformed resumes to <0.1% of sessions. Customer notified and mitigation validated.
resolution_notes: Hotfix rolled to dedicated pool for Lumenary at 2026-03-10T02:10Z.
Linked PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2411 - adds single-writer guard and sequence checks.
Rollback plan existed: re-enable optimistic writes if latency/regression observed; roll forward used after 30-minute stability window.
No data loss detected; all affected sessions were read-only resumes and no persisted customer data deleted.
